claims.text: A single post-processing anneal at approximately 600 °C for about 120 hours under an inert atmosphere is the proposed intervention.
The initial refractory HEA has a continuous ordered matrix.
Annealing the continuous-ordered starting material at 600 °C for 120 hours will transform it into an inverted microstructure.
The inverted microstructure consists of a continuous disordered BCC matrix containing discrete nanoscale B2 precipitates.
The ordered precipitates are coherent with the surrounding matrix.
Annealing promotes controlled diffusion that converts the initially continuous ordered phase into discrete nanoscale precipitates.
The coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature and thereby increase yield strength.
A continuous disordered BCC matrix preserves room-temperature ductility better than a continuous ordered B2 matrix.
The annealed alloy will have approximately 30–40% greater yield strength at about 600 °C than the as-processed continuous-ordered baseline.
The annealed alloy will retain room-temperature ductility similar to that of the as-processed baseline.
The annealing treatment does not alter the alloy's overall elemental makeup.
Because the elemental makeup is unchanged, annealing will cause no significant increase in density.
A continuous ordered B2 matrix can be associated with poor room-temperature compressive ductility.
The continuous-ordered baseline has relatively lower high-temperature mechanical strength than the proposed annealed state.
Excessively long or high-temperature annealing can over-coarsen the precipitates and degrade room-temperature performance.
Excessively aggressive annealing can produce undesirable phase transformations or an increase in density.
The beneficial strength-ductility effect exists only within a narrowly controlled annealing regime.
The optimal annealing temperature, duration, and atmosphere vary among refractory HEA compositions.
Mechanical evaluation should include room-temperature and 600 °C uniaxial testing, with TEM or EBSD used to assess the phase distribution.
